issues.legal_issue: A mortgagee’s possession under a tenancy statute and subsequent purchase of the tenant’s estate do not extinguish the mortgagor’s right to redeem where the mortgage rights are preserved and there is no contract or merger ending the mortgage.
material_facts: The tenant mortgaged the land and later fell into rent arrears.
The mortgagee paid arrears and obtained possession under the tenancy statute, which preserved the mortgagee’s existing rights.
After further arrears, the mortgagee purchased the tenant’s estate at a court sale while already in possession as mortgagee.
The purchase was of the tenant’s estate, not the landlord’s estate, and no contract ending the right to redeem was pleaded.
The High Court granted a preliminary decree for redemption, and the mortgagee appealed.
issues.conclusion: The appeal was dismissed and the decree for redemption was upheld.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 90 of the Trusts Act, the mortgagee in possession held the property subject to the mortgagor’s right to redeem. Section 225 of the Orissa Tenancy Act made the person obtaining possession under it a statutory mortgagee and, under subsection (2), preserved existing mortgage rights. The principle that a mortgage remains a mortgage applies: absent a contract, merger, court order, or special statutory provision ending redemption, the mortgagee’s purchase of the tenant’s estate did not extinguish the right to redeem. No earlier cases were cited.

rule.if: appeal_from_redemption_decree and mortgagee_in_possession and possession_under_tenancy_law and statute_preserves_mortgage_rights and mortgagee_purchased_tenant_estate and not contract_ended_redemption and not mortgage_merged_into_higher_estate

predicates.appeal_from_redemption_decree: A party appeals from a decree granting redemption of mortgaged property.
predicates.mortgagee_in_possession: The mortgagee holds possession of the mortgaged property in the capacity of mortgagee.
predicates.possession_under_tenancy_law: The mortgagee obtained possession under a tenancy-law mechanism.
predicates.statute_preserves_mortgage_rights: The governing law preserves the mortgagee’s existing mortgage rights after possession is obtained.
predicates.mortgagee_purchased_tenant_estate: The mortgagee later purchased the tenant’s estate at a court sale while holding possession as mortgagee.
predicates.contract_ended_redemption: The parties made an agreement ending the mortgagor’s right to redeem.
predicates.mortgage_merged_into_higher_estate: The mortgagee acquired a higher estate into which the mortgage merged.

issues.definition: When the stated appeal and property circumstances apply, the mortgagor retains the right to redeem.

issues.legal_issue: The parties may be directed to bear their own costs where the circumstances include the plaintiffs’ responsibility for the default and their failure to substantiate an allegation of fraud.
material_facts: The rent was allowed to fall into arrears, leading to proceedings and the sale of the property.
The plaintiffs alleged that the later transactions were fraudulent, but that allegation was not substantiated.
issues.conclusion: Each party was ordered to bear its own costs throughout.
issues.legal_principle: The court allocated costs in light of the circumstances, including the plaintiffs’ responsibility for allowing the rent to fall into arrears and their unsuccessful allegation of fraud. No provision or earlier case was cited for this costs direction.

predicates.appeal_from_property_dispute: A party appeals in a dispute concerning rights to property.
predicates.plaintiffs_allowed_obligations_to_fall_i: The plaintiffs allowed payments required to preserve their property rights to fall into arrears.
predicates.plaintiffs_unsuccessfully_alleged_fraud: The plaintiffs alleged fraud in the relevant transactions but failed to substantiate that allegation.

issues.definition: When an appeal in a property dispute involves both the plaintiffs’ responsibility for arrears and their unsupported fraud allegation, each party bears its own costs.
